subject: Nanotechnology
title: Radiative Cooling Nanostructures
description: A micro-lesson that makes Radiative Cooling Nanostructures usable.

hook.text: Cool a building without electricity — nanostructured surfaces radiate heat into space through the atmosphere's IR window.

buildup.text: The atmosphere is transparent between 8 and 13 micrometers — surfaces emitting in this band lose heat to outer space.

discovery.text: Multilayer nano-photonic films are engineered to emit maximally in the sky window while reflecting all sunlight.

twist.text: On humid days the atmospheric window narrows — water vapor absorbs some of the emitted radiation, reducing cooling.

climax.text: SkyCool Systems commercialized radiative cooling panels — cutting building AC costs by 20% in California trials.

punchline.text: A nano-designed surface cools itself by beaming heat into outer space.

quiz.question: How do radiative cooling nanostructures lower temperature without electricity?
options: They absorb cold from the atmosphere
They emit infrared radiation through the atmospheric transparency window directly into outer space
They block all sunlight from reaching the surface
